title: Dead to Sin, Alive in Christ
summary: The very idea of continuing in sin should revolt a Christian. Your old self is buried, and you have been raised to walk in newness of life.
exhortation: Romans 6 may be one of my favorite chapters in the whole Bible. I think back to times in my life when sin was enveloping and crushing me and seemed impossible to overcome, and this passage has been such a comfort to come back to, memorize and study.

The first thing that jumps out at me is how Paul frames it, almost incredulous: "Are we to continue in sin? By no means!" The idea is revolting and offensive to him. How could I continue in sin? So when I'm fighting sin in my own life, I'm comforted that if my heart grieves over it and doesn't want to live that way anymore, that is exactly the posture Paul says our hearts should have. The very idea of wanting to continue in sin is unthinkable for a Christian.

Second, Paul's argument is not, "Buckle down, folks. Let's launch a sin-killing campaign." His argument is, "Don't you understand that you died with Christ? Your old self is dead. It was buried. It's six feet under."

And then he ends with this glorious truth: your old self isn't just buried. You are raised with Christ. You have a new nature and a new life in Jesus. So as we walk through our day, through sin and temptation but also through the trials and weariness of life, let's remember that the old self has been buried and the new self is raised with Christ.
prayer: Lord, we have the victory in you, Jesus. By the power of your Spirit we can walk in victory over sin and over this world, and even in death we have the victory through Jesus.

As we look at the day ahead, I pray for anyone who is discouraged over their failures and sins. Remind them of their victory in you, Jesus: their sins have been paid for, the old is dead and the new has come. Let us walk in newness of life, and find the peace that surpasses understanding and the joy of our salvation. In Jesus' name, amen.
